headline: Hopefully, they will show all the good things
dek: The President will be on “60 Minutes” tonight, and hopes the programme will show everything good done in two years, and asks the Republican Senate for help.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I will be interviewed tonight on “60 Minutes.” Hopefully, they will show all the good things we’ve done over the past 2 years, not even including the First Term, which was incredible. If we get help from the Republican Senate, we can still do things that are unbelievable! President DJT

verification.note: Copied by the editor from truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 8 November 2026 (shown as 8:01 AM Pacific).

en: Tonight I will sit down with 60 Minutes. I welcome the chance to answer hard questions and to speak directly to the American people about the work of the past two years: what we have achieved, and what remains to be done.
With the support of the Senate, there is still a great deal we can accomplish together, and I intend to make that case.
fr: Ce soir, je serai l’invité de l’émission 60 Minutes. Je me réjouis de pouvoir répondre à des questions exigeantes et de m’adresser directement aux Américains sur le travail des deux dernières années : ce que nous avons accompli, et ce qu’il reste à faire.
Avec le soutien du Sénat, nous pouvons encore accomplir beaucoup ensemble, et j’entends le démontrer.

text: Ce soir, il passe à « 60 Minutes ». Il espère qu’on montrera tout ce qu’il a fait de bien en deux ans, sans compter le premier mandat, « incroyable ».

Chez nous, une montre, on ne la juge pas sur ce que l’horloger en dit à la télévision : on la porte quelques années, et on voit si elle retarde. Soixante minutes, c’est d’ailleurs exactement le temps qu’il faut pour le vérifier.
en: He’s on “60 Minutes” tonight, and hopes they’ll show all the good things he’s done in two years, not even counting the first term, which was “incredible”.

Round here, we don’t judge a watch by what the watchmaker says about it on television: we wear it for a few years and see whether it runs slow. Sixty minutes, by the way, is exactly how long it takes to check.

text: Salut les gaillards ! Ce soir je passe à la télé, à « 60 Minutes ». J’espère qu’ils montreront tout le bon travail.

Chez nous, une heure, c’est juste le temps d’une fondue moitié-moitié. Et le meilleur, c’est à la fin : la religieuse, au fond du caquelon. Alors gardez le meilleur pour la fin, et demandez un coup de main au Sénat, comme on demande au voisin de passer le pain.
en: Hey folks! I’m on TV tonight, on “60 Minutes”. I hope they’ll show all the good work.

Round here, an hour is just the time it takes to eat a fondue. And the best part comes last: the crispy crust of cheese at the bottom of the pot. So save the best for the end, and ask the Senate for a hand, the way you’d ask your neighbour to pass the bread.
fr: “La religieuse” is the golden crust of cheese left at the bottom of the fondue pot (the caquelon); in Romandy, it is the most coveted bite.

text: Ce soir, « 60 Minutes » à la télé. Il espère qu’ils montreront le bon côté.
Ici, on dit qu’il faut attendre la fin de la marée pour savoir ce que la mer a laissé sur la plage. Deux ans de bilan en une heure, c’est court. Mais bon, s’il fait beau à la télé, c’est déjà ça.
en: “60 Minutes” on TV tonight. He hopes they’ll show the good side.
Here we say you have to wait for the tide to go out to see what the sea has left on the beach. Two years of record in one hour is short. Still, if the weather’s fine on telly, that’s something.

text: Ce soir, il passe à « 60 Minutes ». Il espère qu’on montrera tout le bon.

À Lyon, on a une règle : on ne juge pas un bouchon sur sa devanture, on le juge sur son tablier de sapeur. Alors qu’il montre l’assiette, pas la carte. Et s’il lui faut l’aide du Sénat pour finir, qu’il commande un deuxième pot.
en: He’s on “60 Minutes” tonight. He hopes they’ll show all the good stuff.

In Lyon we have a rule: you don’t judge a bistro by its shop front, you judge it by its signature dish. So show us the plate, not the menu. And if he needs the Senate’s help to finish, he can order a second jug.
fr: The tablier de sapeur, breaded and fried tripe, is a Lyon bistro classic; a “pot” is the 46-centilitre bottle of house wine.

text: So he’s doing 60 Minutes tonight and hoping they only show the good stuff? Love the optimism. Out here we call that a highlight reel, and we have entire companies that make those.
Real talk, though: the best interviews are the ones where they ask the hard questions. Growth mindset, you know?
en: California likes the optimism, but notes that “only showing the good parts” is what an edited highlight reel does, not a news interview.
Its friendly advice: welcome the hard questions; that is where an interview is worth watching.

text: Oh, he’s going to be on 60 Minutes tonight? Well, isn’t that something. We’ll probably catch it after supper.

Now, hoping they only show the good parts, that’s a pretty big ask of a news program, but you never know. And asking the Senate for help is just being a good neighbor. Or it would be, if he asked a little nicer.
en: The Midwest will politely watch after dinner.
It gently points out that a news programme rarely shows only the good parts, and that asking for help works better when you ask nicely.

text: On 60 Minutes tonight, hoping they show all the good bits. Fair enough, we’d all like that.
But in Manchester we know how telly works: you give them an hour, they keep twelve minutes, and the twelve they keep are the ones where you said something daft.
en: Manchester understands wanting a flattering interview.
But it knows how television editing works: hours are recorded, a few minutes are kept, and those are rarely the ones you would have chosen.

text: His Majesty’s Government notes that the President will appear this evening on a respected American current affairs programme, and trusts that the exchange will be as illuminating as these occasions so often are.
We would observe, gently, that one rarely chooses which parts of an interview are broadcast. That, after all, is rather the point of a free press.
en: He wants the programme to show only the good bits.
That is not how journalism works, and we think that is a good thing.

text: France welcomes every opportunity for a head of state to account for his record before a free press. An hour of questions on national television is a demanding exercise, and a healthy one for democracy.
We would only add, in friendship, that history tends to judge a record over decades rather than in a single broadcast, however well edited.
fr: La France salue toute occasion donnée à un chef d’État de rendre compte de son action devant une presse libre. Une heure de questions à la télévision nationale est un exercice exigeant, et salutaire pour la démocratie.
Nous ajouterons seulement, en toute amitié, que l’Histoire juge un bilan sur des décennies plutôt qu’en une seule émission, si bien montée soit-elle.

text: The Federal Council has taken note of this television interview.

In Switzerland, the President of the Confederation changes every year, which leaves little time for a two-year retrospective. Our record is set out in the Federal Council’s annual report to Parliament: several hundred pages, rarely broadcast in prime time.
fr: Le Conseil fédéral prend acte de cette interview télévisée.

En Suisse, le président de la Confédération change chaque année, ce qui laisse peu de temps pour un bilan sur deux ans. Notre bilan figure dans le rapport de gestion annuel du Conseil fédéral au Parlement : plusieurs centaines de pages, rarement diffusées en prime time.
notes: The presidency of the Swiss Confederation rotates every year among the seven members of the Federal Council.
